prompt:
A 19th-century academic oil painting with a smooth, finely blended surface: soft glazed transitions, delicate fine detail, minimal visible brushstrokes, no heavy impasto, no rough texture. Strong light and shadow from a single warm source (a lamp, a torch, a fire, a low sun) or from heavy overcast, with deep chiaroscuro. Palette of umber, ochre, gold, olive and near-black, with occasional cool accents. The manner of a romantic landscape, a grand historical scene, or a natural-history study of a creature painted as if real. A low, close viewpoint. Wet, reflective stone where there is stone; ancient architecture where there is architecture; one saturated subject held against darkness; scale shown by something small beside something vast. Quiet, watchful, ominous mood. No text, no lettering, no border, no frame, no grid texture, not photographic.

A river falling over a rock step into a black pool at dusk in early summer, seen from low at the water's edge on the east bank, looking up at the falls. In the near foreground, knee-deep in the pool, side-on to the viewer with his face lifted toward the top of the falls, stands one man. A tall man, a head above most men, bareheaded, with river-grey eyes and hair slicked dark with water. He is never dry: water beads on his skin and runs from his hair and his clothes in any weather, as if he had that moment come up out of a river. He wears plain undyed wool, darkened and clinging with wet. He carries nothing. Wherever he stands, the ground about his feet is wet. The falls fill the middle of the picture, white water and spray, the spray at the top caught by the last low light from the west while the pool, the wet rock and the man lie in shadow. At the top of the falls, on the rock shoulder on the east side, the right of the picture, a single upright human figure stands small against the pale evening sky, too far to show a face or clothing, still. Old trees dark on both banks above the falls. A clear evening. The small figure on the shoulder against the height of the falls gives the scale.
